record.original_question: Given a function f in a weighted Hardy space H^2_omega such that its polynomial multiples are dense in the space, and given zeta in the unit circle T, is there a sector with vertex at zeta that is devoid of zeros of the optimal polynomial approximants to 1/f? More generally, are there regions or rays that the zeros avoid?

evidence.quote: A function f in H^2_omega is called cyclic if its polynomial multiples are dense in the space.

Given a function f in H^2_omega not identically 0 and n in N, we define the n-th optimal polynomial approximant of 1/f in H^2_omega to be the polynomial q_n that minimizes ||pf - 1||_omega among all polynomials p of degree at most n.

Open Question 2. Given a cyclic function f in H^2_omega, and given zeta in T, is there a sector with vertex at zeta that is devoid of zeros of opas? More generally, are there regions or rays that the zeros avoid?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega = (\omega_k)_{k\geq 0}$ be a sequence of positive weights, and let $H^2_\omega$ denote the weighted Hardy space of analytic functions $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k z^k$ on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ with norm $\|f\|_\omega^2 = \sum_{k=0}^\infty |a_k|^2 \omega_k < \infty$. A function $f \in H^2_\omega$ is called cyclic if the set of polynomial multiples $\{p f : p \text{ polynomial}\}$ is dense in $H^2_\omega$. For a non-identically-zero $f \in H^2_\omega$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th optimal polynomial approximant of $1/f$ is the polynomial $q_n$ of degree at most $n$ that minimizes $\|p f - 1\|_\omega$ over all polynomials $p$ of degree at most $n$.

Question: Given a cyclic function $f \in H^2_\omega$ and a point $\zeta \in \mathbb{T} = \partial\mathbb{D}$, does there exist an open sector with vertex at $\zeta$ that contains no zeros of any of the optimal polynomial approximants $q_n$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$? More generally, characterize the regions or rays in the complex plane that are avoided by the zeros of the sequence $(q_n)_{n\geq 0}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2021 survey on optimal polynomial approximants. Subsequent work (e.g., results on equidistribution of zeros on the unit circle for certain cyclic polynomial generators, and electrostatic/OPUC-based analyses from 2022–2025) has produced partial results in special cases but no general resolution of the sector/zero-avoidance problem for arbitrary cyclic functions in weighted Hardy spaces has been reported. The problem appears to remain open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of zeros of some polynomials related to cyclic functions
status_evidence.snippet: For polynomial generators without zeros inside the disk but with some zeros on its boundary, the weakly asymptotic distribution of the zeros is the uniform measure on the unit circle.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on the asymptotic distribution of zeros of OPAs are known in special cases, but do not resolve the general sector/zero-avoidance question.

status_evidence.title: Optimal polynomial approximants and orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle - electrostatic approach
status_evidence.snippet: A link is established between optimal polynomial approximants and orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle, with an electrostatic interpretation of the zeros.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work provides new tools for studying zero locations of OPAs but does not settle the general sector-avoidance question.

status_evidence.title: Metric projections, zeros of optimal polynomial approximants, and some extremal problems in Hardy spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies zeros of optimal polynomial approximants and related extremal problems.
status_evidence.claim: Continued recent research on zeros of OPAs indicates the topic remains an active open area.
